standard.title: Aesthetic qualities of texts
standard.description: analyse and evaluate the aesthetic qualities of texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students analyse the effect of complex literary devices and evaluate an author's literary style (AC9E9LE04, AC9E9LE05). They have not yet analysed and evaluated the aesthetic qualities of texts using literary analysis terminology.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse and evaluate the aesthetic qualities of texts.

nodes.label: Identifying aesthetic qualities and valued aspects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify aesthetic qualities in a text using appropriate literary analysis terminology, explaining what is valued about those aspects.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two aesthetic qualities in a text using appropriate literary terms and explain why those aspects are valued.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe a range of aesthetic qualities across a literary text — using terms such as 'stanza', 'figurative language', 'symbolism', 'soundtrack' — explaining what is valued about each aspect.
wider: Compare aesthetic qualities across texts from different cultural traditions, examining how different traditions value different aesthetic qualities
Examine how First Nations Australian aesthetic traditions are expressed in literary texts and what criteria of value apply
Analyse how aesthetic judgements about a text have shifted over time as cultural values have changed
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to evaluate aesthetic qualities using literary analysis terms — without an adequate vocabulary repertoire, evaluative claims cannot be articulated with precision and collapse into vague impressions.

response_modes.reason: Literary analysis terminology must be accumulated through encounters with diverse texts — students need to build a working repertoire of aesthetic vocabulary they can deploy with precision in novel analytical contexts.

success_criteria: Identifies at least two aesthetic qualities using appropriate literary analysis terms
Explains why those qualities are valued in the context of the text

nodes.label: Evaluating aesthetic qualities with supported analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the aesthetic qualities of a text, making supported judgements about the use and effect of specific literary devices.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate the use and effect of at least one literary device (e.g. symbolism) in a text, making a supported judgement.
nodes.typical_width: Evaluate the aesthetic qualities of a literary text, analysing and evaluating the use of multiple literary devices and making supported judgements about their contribution to the text's overall aesthetic effect.
wider: Evaluate how an author's aesthetic choices across a text create a distinctive style, comparing with other authors' approaches to the same genre or form
Evaluate the aesthetic qualities of a First Nations Australian text on its own terms, considering the aesthetic traditions from which it draws
Write a published-style review of a literary text that evaluates aesthetic qualities for a specific audience

response_modes.reason: Evaluation of aesthetic qualities requires students to articulate a reasoned basis for their judgement — not just whether they found something effective but why, with reference to specific textual evidence and literary criteria.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Aesthetic evaluation is rich across diverse literary traditions — the contrast between Western literary criteria and First Nations Australian aesthetic traditions offers particularly meaningful depth.
success_criteria: Makes a supported judgement about the use and effect of at least one literary device
Uses specific textual evidence to support the aesthetic evaluation
